inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 securities report, consolidated statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payment transactions' 370 (JPY millions); equity-award cash taxes nil (restricted stock + share options, no net-share settlement disclosed)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close, Friday 30 Oct 15:30 JST; not an after-hours print)
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 1,504,481,403 less treasury 47,819,230 at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin) = 1,456.66m, plus 2.476m dilutive (share acquisition rights 2,286k + restricted stock 190k, FY2026 diluted-EPS table) = 1,459.1m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The Metrics.csv 1,504.0m is the FY2026 weighted-average diluted count, stale after the JPY111.7bn FY2026 buyback and the 127m-share cancellation. No buyback in Q1 FY2027 (cash flow shows 0).
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + beta 1.25 (diversified chemicals/cyclical materials) x Japan ERP 6.0% = cost of equity ~9.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt 2.0% (FY2026 interest paid JPY17.4bn on JPY862bn bonds and borrowings), 1.4% after tax. Market weights at 30 June 2026 balance sheet and current price: equity ~JPY1,720bn (67%), debt JPY862bn (33%). WACC = 0.67 x 9.2 + 0.33 x 1.4 = 6.6%, used as 6.5% in ALL three scenarios. Cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. IFRS 16 filer: lease principal repayments JPY13,028m (FY2026 financing) plus estimated lease interest ~JPY1,000m (JPY41.6bn liabilities at ~2.5%) = ~JPY14.0bn = 0.55% of revenue, charged as lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT. Lease liabilities (11,711 current + 27,835 non-current = 39,546 at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from total_debt/net_debt. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (~JPY13bn): 131,615 - 13,000 = ~118,600 = 4.6% of revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: NCI book value JPY130,798m at 30 June 2026 deducted via equity_bridge; flows are consolidated. NCI earned JPY9.9bn of FY2026 profit (11% of profit), so book (6.7% of total equity) is a fair deduction.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Matching-asset rule: operating income (the EBITDA base) EXCLUDES share of profit of equity-method associates (JPY21.5bn FY2026, JPY-2.4bn FY2025 after impairments) and finance income (JPY8.6bn, of which interest received 4.1bn and dividends on cross-shareholdings ~4.4bn). Their source assets therefore enter the bridge: equity-method investments at book JPY191,597m (30 June 2026) and FVOCI equity instruments at an estimated JPY127.3bn at 30 June 2026 (fair value 140,255 at 31 March 2026 per yuho Note 16, reduced by the full 12.9bn fall in non-current other financial assets over the quarter, i.e. conservatively assuming the whole decline was the equity portfolio). Interest received on the JPY260bn cash is also outside the flows; cash is netted in net_debt, so there is no double count. Assets held for sale (JPY36.6bn, liabilities 7.7bn) are a Darwin-Project disposal; their earnings remain in the flows until sold and the proceeds are not added -- immaterial either way. Net retirement benefit asset (90.1bn asset vs 74.0bn liability) ignored.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted -- routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Not a bank/REIT/LIC: Toray is a diversified materials manufacturer (fibers, performance chemicals, carbon fiber composites, water treatment, life science). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Mid-cycle normalisation: Toray books 'non-core' charges nearly every year (FY2026 operating income 97.2bn vs core 141.9bn after the Korean battery-separator impairment; FY2025 127.5bn vs 142.8bn), so the EBITDA margin path is anchored to reported EBITDA (10-yr average 10.1%) rather than core EBITDA (10.4-10.6%), i.e. ~0.5pt/yr of recurring impairment/restructuring is treated as a real cost. FY2027 guidance (maintained at the Aug 2026 Q1 release; H1 raised to revenue 1,390bn / core OI 87bn / NPAT 45bn): revenue 2,830bn (+9.5%), core OI 160bn, NPAT 90bn, at USD/JPY 150-155 -- the base year-1 growth and margin follow it. Cash tax 29% on operating EBIT: statutory 30.6% less R&D credit and foreign rate differential, plus withholding on foreign dividends; FY2026 cash taxes paid of 75.6bn were abnormal (vs 30-42bn in FY2023-25) and are not carried forward. Working capital: receivables 621 + inventories 576 - payables 316 = JPY881bn = 34% of revenue, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is negative (-20% base, below the structural 34% because part of guided FY2027 growth is yen-translation rather than volume). SBC is 0.014% of revenue and is projected at 0%: house and street bases coincide, so the band collapses (band_position should be read as n/a). Buybacks of JPY111.7bn in FY2026 funded the flat count -- Toray is a repurchaser. Price is the TSE regular close; H1 FY2027 results due early November 2026 are the next anchor refresh (the full-year forecast is likely to be revised then).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: blend of FY2027 guidance (+9.5%, part yen-translation) fading to ~2% nominal; the 10-year revenue CAGR FY2016-FY2026 is 2.1% and the 5-year figures (revenue 6.5%, EPS 13.1%, equity 7.8%) are measured from the FY2021 COVID trough and inflated by yen depreciation on translation of overseas subsidiaries
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.8% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 13.1% diverge by >30%; both are trough-based (FY2021 EPS 28.57, the lowest in a decade). Owner-FCF CAGRs (3yr +15.1%, 5yr -6.1%) are noise: reported FCF ranged -24bn to +98bn over FY2016-FY2026 on capex timing and working capital, not on a trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) less SBC; SBC is 355-403m/yr so the adjustment is immaterial. Interest income not stripped (net debt positive). FY2016-FY2019 are J-GAAP; FY2020 onward IFRS, so the 10-yr revenue CAGR straddles a standard change (IFRS restatement cut FY2020 revenue vs the J-GAAP basis).

base.narrative: FY2027 lands on guidance (revenue +9.5% to 2,830bn, core OI 160bn => core EBITDA ~10.4%, ~10.0% after the usual ~0.5pt of non-core charges). Growth fades to ~2% nominal JPY. IGNITION 2028 portfolio pruning lifts the mix by ~0.5pt to a 10.5% mature EBITDA margin. Capex runs ~1.15x D&A (history 1.1-1.2x) and settles at 5.3% of revenue; cash tax 29%; working capital consumes 20% of incremental revenue. Terminal 14x owner FCF (cyclical cap; Gordon at 6.5%/2.0% would be 22.7x).

bull.narrative: FY2027 beats (the H1 upgrade carries into H2; revenue +11%), the aerospace carbon-fiber ramp (Boeing rates, defence, space) continues through FY2029, Performance Chemicals films ride the AI/MLCC capex cycle, and the Darwin Project actually exits the structural-reform businesses (battery separator film, sub-scale pharma), lifting EBITDA margin to 12% by FY2032 with no further impairments. Capex discipline under the ROIC KPI brings capex/D&A toward 1.1x. Terminal 15x.

bear.narrative: FY2027 misses the H2 of guidance as Middle East feedstock inflation and a stronger yen (guidance assumes 150-155) bite; FY2028 is a down-cycle year (revenue -4%) with auto resins and industrial carbon fiber (pressure vessels, wind) still unrecovered and another structural-reform impairment, pushing EBITDA margin to 8.4% (FY2024 trough was 7.6%). Apparel fibers keep losing share to Chinese producers; margin recovers only to 9.0%. Capex cannot flex below 5.6% on an ageing asset base. Terminal 12x, growth 1.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-anchored FY2027 (+9.5% revenue, ~10% EBITDA margin net of recurring non-core charges), fading to 2% nominal growth and a 10.5% mature margin as IGNITION 2028 prunes the portfolio. Owner FCF margin matures at ~2.6% of revenue, consistent with the 10-year unlevered history (~2.7%). The axes are the aerospace carbon-fiber cycle, Performance Chemicals' exposure to auto and China, and whether the ROIC programme converts into cash rather than more impairments.
scenario_narratives.bull: Aerospace ramp plus AI-related films plus genuine exits from structural-reform businesses lift the mature EBITDA margin to 12%; FY2027 beats and growth stays above 4% for three years. Needs three independent things to go right (aero, electronics cycle, Darwin execution).
scenario_narratives.bear: Yen reversal and a FY2028 auto/industrial downcycle with another impairment; margin troughs at 8.4% and recovers only to 9%. No solvency question (net debt/EBITDA ~2.3x, JPY debt at 2%), so this is an earnings-and-multiple bear, not a survival one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): Toray's non-core charges have recurred in every year of the IFRS history and the earnings base swings with the auto, aerospace and yen cycles -- a down-year is a normal event, not a tail. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull case needs the aerospace ramp, an electronics-film upcycle and Darwin-Project exits to all land, and the company's own record under AP-G 2025 was persistent low ROIC. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Toray is valued as a mid-cycle cash generator, not on its core-operating-income narrative: EBITDA of ~10-10.5% of revenue converts to only ~2.5% owner FCF after lease cost, capex at ~1.15x D&A, 29% cash tax and working capital that grows with revenue. The house DCF discounts those flows at a JPY WACC of 6.5%, caps the terminal at 12-15x FCF for a cyclical, and adds the equity-method and cross-shareholding portfolios (whose income is outside the flows) while deducting NCI and JPY602bn of net debt. The market, by contrast, prices Toray at ~0.95x book and ~8.5x core EBITDA; the gap between that and the FCF-based value is the price of a re-rating thesis (ROIC reform under IGNITION 2028) that the cash flows have not yet earned.
valuation_philosophy.no_re_rate_memo: At Toray's own historical EV/EBITDA of ~7-9x applied to terminal EBITDA (~JPY350bn), the terminal value would be roughly 2.5x the house 14x-FCF terminal and the per-share value would sit near JPY1,000 -- close to the current price. That is the multiple the market extends to a Japanese conglomerate on book value and reform hope; the house basis is the cash the business produces at a 6.5% discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: FCF conversion: a 1pt change in mature EBITDA margin moves owner FCF by ~0.7% of revenue, roughly a quarter of the terminal FCF
Capex/D&A ratio: capex has averaged 5.9% of revenue over ten years vs 5.3% assumed at maturity; reverting to 5.9% removes most of the terminal FCF
Yen: FY2027 guidance assumes USD/JPY 150-155; ~45-50% of revenue is overseas, so a 10% stronger yen is roughly -5% revenue and more on translated profit
Recurring impairments: the gap between core and reported operating income (JPY15-45bn/yr in FY2025-26) is treated as a real 0.5pt cost; if structural-reform write-downs grow, so does the gap
Bridge items: equity-method investments (JPY192bn) at book and cross-shareholdings (JPY127bn est.) at fair value are 22% of the house equity value; their realisability is a judgment
Terminal multiple: Gordon at 6.5%/2% implies 22.7x FCF; the 14x cap is what keeps the value honest for a cyclical and is itself a judgment
